items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Jack Butler and I along with his wife Raye and Beezie shared an apartment on the side street across from the Kursall.

ctx.x: After a few weeks at the Moulin Rouge, the Cotton Club show moved to the Ambassador Theatre which was next door to where we were playing and sometimes I would see Dicky Wells coming from around the back of the building and he told me that he had been back there listening to our band because he could hear it better than from the side that gave onto the street.

The Cotton Club Show left for England and Willie Lewis' band left for another summer season in Knocke, but George Johnson did not go with the orchestra. I suppose that Willie had engaged him only for the Ambassador job. It was only during engagements at the summer resorts such as Knocke and Ostende that Willie Lewis' orchestra played tea dances or matinees every day. But it was a pleasure to work in the best Negro orchestra in Europe and although we stayed up late most every night, I and some of the other…

Ray Ventura was the leader of the biggest French jazz orchestra in France and he was engaged to play upstairs in the large hall of the Kursall. Ray had an orchestra of about 16 or 17 musicians and an American girl singer whose name I remember as being Betty. Ventura had a real show band, but he also had the best musicians in Europe from different countries. One outstanding musician in the orchestra was a French trumpet player named Philippe Brun.
